Reported home autonomy thus reaches L2, the task level, and remote operation bridges the rest.

Much of what the remote operator supplies is the work of S2. A request such as “get the living room ready for guests, but leave the children’s puzzle on the table” leaves most objects, all steps, and the completion criterion unstated. Fulfilling it requires interpreting what the household wants, deciding where each item belongs, sequencing the work, checking the result, and responding to interruptions. Throughout, the robot must remember the home, its occupants, and their preferences while protecting their privacy. An Embodied S2 that handled such requests would change what a home robot is. It would no longer be an appliance for one chore or a teleoperated body, but a helper to which a household delegates an open list of chores. Remote experts would then approve exceptions rather than perform the work.

B.2 Manufacturing and Logistics

Factories and warehouses are where robots already work at large scale (International Federation of Robotics, 2026; Dresser, 2025), and where the limits of programmed automation are most visible. Industrial arms repeat engineered motions with high speed and precision inside fixtures and cells. This approach pays off in high-volume production but turns every change of product or layout into an engineering project. Humanoids and learned policies are now entering these settings. Figure AI reports that its Figure 02 deployment at BMW ran ten-hour shifts and contributed to the production of more than 30,000 vehicles (Figure AI, 2025a). Apptronik agreed to pilot its Apollo humanoid at Mercedes-Benz, runs data collection at customer sites including Mercedes-Benz, and uses the resulting fleet data to train Gemini Robotics models (Apptronik, 2024; Apptronik, 2026; Gemini Robotics Team, 2025a). Hyundai has announced plans to deploy Boston Dynamics’ Atlas in its plants (Boston Dynamics, 2026b). Skild AI reports more than 60 paying customers ten months after its first commercial deployment; mobility accounts for 10% of its revenue, and the remaining 90% comes mainly from manipulation tasks (Pathak and Gupta, 2026). In logistics, Agility reports that its Digit robots have moved more than 100,000 totes at GXO (Agility Robotics, 2025; GXO Logistics and Agility Robotics, 2026). Amazon reports operating more than a million robots coordinated by what it describes as a fleet foundation model (Dresser, 2025), and its tactile picking robot asks human workers to take over items that it cannot handle (Davies, 2025). All of these figures are company-reported.

Because each cycle in these settings is short and repetitive, Embodied S2 would contribute less within a cycle than around it. It could verify each cycle and handle exceptions such as a jam or an unfamiliar item, diagnosing the cause and then either retrying differently or handing over with a precise report. It could also orchestrate fleets and re-task robots when production changes. Re-tasking may bring the largest gain. An Embodied S2 that composed existing skills into a new sequence from a work instruction, and verified the first parts before running at volume, would turn a reprogramming project into a configuration step. Automation could then extend from high-volume lines to high-mix, low-volume work that fixed automation has rarely reached.

B.3 Inspection

Inspection is an early commercial application of embodied reasoning models, which are candidate S2 foundation models. It suits current models because it tolerates latency and rewards verified reading of physical state, and it illustrates the step from collecting data to making judgments. A conventional inspection robot repeats a preplanned route and records data for people to interpret. Boston Dynamics reports more than 1,500 Spot robots with customers (Boston Dynamics, 2026c) and has integrated Gemini Robotics-ER into its inspection software for reading gauges and interpreting site conditions (Graesser and Xu, 2026; Boston Dynamics, 2026a). Google reports a demonstration in which Gemini 4 Argon controls a real Spot after practicing the task in a simulated twin that it built itself (Rao, 2026). An Embodied S2 could connect reading and control by acting on what it reads. When a gauge is out of range, it could look again from another angle, check the related valve, and file a report with the evidence attached, instead of leaving every anomaly for a person to find in the recordings. At the role level, inspection would also require a persistent model of the site that is updated on every round.

B.4 Healthcare and Laboratories

Hospital delivery robots already navigate elevators and corridors autonomously (Diligent Robotics, 2024), but they carry items between fixed points. An Embodied S2 could turn such a robot into an assistant for varied requests, such as fetching a particular item from a supply room. Eldercare is the most demanding domain considered here. Delegating it to a robot would require responsibility at the role level (L4), long-term memory of a person, well-timed intervention, and the strongest privacy and safety protections. Current evidence is limited to trials.

Laboratory automation has long executed fixed protocols, and structured laboratories also host autonomous research campaigns that run continuously for days. The A-Lab synthesized 36 of 57 target compounds over 17 days of continuous operation (Szymanski et al., 2023), although the novelty of its products and the automated analysis that identified them were later disputed; the count given here is the corrected one (Leeman et al., 2024; Szymanski et al., 2026). A mobile robotic chemist ran 688 experiments over eight days (Burger et al., 2020). These runs show sustained operation in a restricted domain rather than a role held across open-ended work. A language-model agent, Coscientist, has also planned and executed chemistry experiments (Boiko et al., 2023). In open-ended work, an Embodied S2 could decide which experiment to run next given the results so far, verify that each step produced what it should, and record provenance. In laboratories, verification of outcomes, rather than manipulation, is likely to be the bottleneck.

B.5 Agriculture and Mobility

Agricultural robots operate commercially at the primitive level (L1): laser weeders work in 15 countries according to their manufacturer, which reports more than 200 growers across its laser-weeding and tractor-autonomy products (Carbon Robotics, 2026), but each machine performs one job. An Embodied S2 could let one platform scout a field, decide where weeding or harvesting is needed, and switch between these jobs as conditions change. In mobility, robotaxis provide hundreds of thousands of paid rides per week in restricted operating domains (Korosec, 2026). Cars and drones are physical agents as well, and the same S2–S1–S0 organization applies to them. Their history also suggests how agentic robotics is likely to scale: domain by domain, with each operating domain widened only as evidence of safety accumulates.

Common Patterns.

Across these domains, evidence of unaided work in unstructured settings is strongest at L2. Some demonstrations extend toward workflows, but their reports do not yet establish all the conditions needed for a reliable L3 claim. Longer operation has been reported only in structured or restricted domains, and wherever the fallback is disclosed, it is a person. The same three changes recur: work assigned by instruction rather than by engineering or new data, supervision by exception rather than one operator per robot, and responsibility extended from single tasks to workflows and roles. Each change would widen the range of work for which deploying a robot is worthwhile. The research directions in Section 6.2 address what delivering these changes would take.

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.

Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a list of packages that need conversion, and welcome developer contributions.
